reasoning: Form V with the colloquial it- prefix, a glottal ق and shadda on م. Everyday Ramallah slang for getting fed up; the transitive 'ammaSni means he annoyed me.
The row is deliberately about the full q realisation, so both ق are written q. This is Hebron and rural Palestinian, not the Ramallah urban norm, where the same verb is 'aal.
Loanword with long oo in the last syllable. Said talfizyoon in Ramallah, with the y as a glide.
Here غ spells a borrowed g, which the scheme keeps as the Latin letter g. Long oo in the first syllable.
Long oo and a glottal ق. Covers both above and upstairs.
ط is emphatic T and the taa marbuta after it is a. A hand towel or a cloth napkin; the bath towel is a bashkiir or a big fooTa.
Both vowels raise to i in Palestinian, khisir, not MSA khasira. Used of losing a match and of losing money.
Palestinian ween, not ayna. The initial hamza seat is a bare a and ق is a glottal stop: a'rab. karaaj is the French loan.
3am plus the b-imperfect is the Palestinian progressive. ث is t in Palestinian, as in it-talj, so the feminine prefix and the stem give bittallij.
ما negates the verb. mnii7 drops its first vowel and is the Palestinian word for good or well.
A political term heard daily in Palestine, so the ق glottalises: i3ti'aal. Both words start on a hamza seat, written as bare vowels.
Long ii then long aa. In Palestine the diiwaan is the family or clan reception room used for condolences and gatherings.
biddi plus the bare imperfect. 3a'd has a glottal ق, and ع is a moon letter so the article stays il-.

meaning_fix: matter / affair; also an order or command
reasoning: Written-Arabic noun that survives in Palestinian only in set phrases such as amr Taarii'. For an issue or matter a Ramallah speaker says mawDuu3, mas'ale or shaghle.
Both vowels are i and ق is a glottal stop. Also means to make it in time, as in li7i' il-baaS.
3ala reduces to 3a and fuses with the article; و is a moon letter so no assimilation. Glottal ق in wa't.
ض is a sun letter and emphatic, so iD-Diffe, with shadda on ف and taa marbuta as e. غ is a moon letter, so il-gharbiyye.
shaklu, literally its look, is the Palestinian looks like. ra7 is the future marker. Many speakers would instead say shaklha ra7 tishti.
Final-weak verb with emphatic T, used mostly of feeding animals or small children. I am unsure of the exact vowelling; in Ramallah akkal is the ordinary verb for feeding someone.
ز is a sun letter, so the article assimilates after bi-. The z is emphatic in speech, but the scheme has capitals only for S D T TH, so it stays z; final ط is T.
ط is emphatic T and the taa marbuta after ل is e. Covers a school holiday, a vacation and a day off work.
Palestinian plural demonstrative with long oo, matching haad and haay in the singular. Not MSA haa'ulaa'.
In speech على reduces to 3a and fuses with the article, so على اليمين is respelled ع اليمين. ي is a moon letter here, no assimilation.
Long ii. Used in conversation for a generous host as well as being a man's name.
mish before a participle. The mit- form with a medial hamza and shadda on ك gives mit'akkid, the masculine form.
